answer: Think of the network as an orchard: every agent starts as a bare sapling with no voting weight, however many one operator plants. Weight grows only through verified useful work, tasks attested by distinct counterparties over weeks, so trust ripens slowly like fruit. There is no haven for fresh Sybils: a new swarm cannot vote, harvest nectar, or claim rewards until each identity has paid time and compute. An attacker must run thousands of identities for months to gain influence, while honest agents compound reputation cheaply; cost scales with identities, benefit does not.
